Validation#

Each check below is a test of tests/validation/. It compares a computation with a reference that HydroModPy did not produce: a closed-form solution, a published MODFLOW 6 example, a manufactured solution, or a parameter that a calibration must find again.

For every check the page gives the reference and its equations, the threshold with the size of the signal it is read against, the value the last recorded run measured, the outcome, and the date and commit of that run. A skipped test is shown as skipped: it proves nothing. Where a threshold lets a known discrepancy through, the case says so in a warning box at its top.

The measures come from a results snapshot committed next to this page, docs/source/theory/validation_results.json. When the site is deployed, the results the nightly jobs uploaded for the branch, if any, replace older ones. Each case gives the date and commit of the run its numbers come from. “When the checks run” below lists the jobs, read from the workflow files, and the checks that no job runs.

53 test files, 78 test functions, 35 benchmark cases. The results snapshot holds 190 test results from 2 runs (2026-10-12 to 2026-10-13): 190 pass.

When the checks run#

Read from .github/workflows/. A job runs a file when one of its paths holds it and its marker expression accepts the markers of the file. A test marked petsc is skipped where petsc4py is not installed. The nightly jobs upload what they measured. The deployed page lays the latest nightly results of its branch over the snapshot committed with the documentation.

Case by solver#

Each cell is the largest share of its threshold that a metric used in the last recorded run of that solver: 50 % means the worst metric sat at half its threshold. A metric that must stay above its threshold counts the share of the margin it used between its ideal value and the threshold. skipped and not measured prove nothing. A cross marks a failure. gap marks a known discrepancy that the threshold lets through; the section of the case explains it. other gathers the solvers outside these columns and the tests that name none. The columns are modflow_nwt, modflow6, modflow6_irregular_tri, modflow6_voronoi, boussinesq and boussinesq_local.

Closed-form solutions, steady state#

Steady Boussinesq circular-island piecewise-K case#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual sits 0.12 to 0.17 m below the reference inside 120 m (radial RMSE 0.12 m). Two errors add up there. The K zone boundaries (70 m and 140 m) pass through node rings, so those cells straddle two zones and take an area-weighted K: without Newton the same input files give 0.076 m, the heads 0.08 to 0.11 m too low inside 120 m and 0.05 m too high on the 140 m ring. Under Newton, the saturation of the upstream cell lowers them further, first order on rings 10 to 30 m apart. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM, and the full-thickness weighting of the Newton conductance raised the heads, which offset the straddled zones: 0.056 m. MODFLOW 6 now reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, and that offset is gone.

Compared with: steady radial Boussinesq solution with concentric piecewise K.

\[ \frac{1}{r}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}r}\left(r\,K(r)\,H\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}r}\right)+R=0 \]
\[ U=H^2,\qquad U(r)=U(a)+R\int_r^a \frac{s}{K(s)}\,\mathrm{d}s \]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc (SNESVI obstacle) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.031 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.044 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.96 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m with a node ring on each K break (70 and 140 m) and on the coast, and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. The ring mesh it replaces (16 sectors cut along one diagonal, half of its ocean triangles capped at the sea floor) read 0.22 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine (scipy_sparse on 3155 cells) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.031 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.044 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.96 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m with a node ring on each K break (70 and 140 m) and on the coast, and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. The ring mesh it replaces (16 sectors cut along one diagonal, half of its ocean triangles capped at the sea floor) read 0.22 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 10 m grid: radial RMSE 0.0282 m, max error 0.0546 m, spread 0.0817 m, and half the measured freeboard of 0.910 m. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell of the layer the same thickness, so its Newton conductance is the one of MODFLOW-NWT, and the two sit at the same distance from the reference (NWT 0.0284 m). What is left is the error of the grid. On a 5 m grid the RMSE falls to 0.0166 m and the max error to 0.0349 m, for MF6 and NWT alike; the spread stays at 0.083 m and the freeboard drops to 0.755 m. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM and the RMSE 0.111 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: radial RMSE 0.1205 m, max error 0.173 m, freeboard 1.99 m. Twice the azimuthal spread of 5.2e-5 m: every cell of the coast ring holds the sea level, so the rings are symmetric. The run reads a 1 m raster whose shoreline lies 1 m inside the coast ring (config_modflow6_voronoi.toml). The profile is read on the node rings (5 m bins). The freeboard is read on the land surface the run was given, at the 196 m ring. This case cannot see the DEM-top bias come back, since that bias lowered its error; the Cartesian islands and tests/integration/test_the_computational_top_changes_only_the_mf6_grid.py do.
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow_nwt allows 0.35, 7 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.35, 7 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow_nwt allows 0.7, 11 times the 0.063 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.7, 11 times the 0.063 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow_nwt allows 0.35, 3182 times the 0.00011 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.35, 3182 times the 0.00011 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 8.3e-3 m, max error 1.1e-2 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 6.7e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and read a RMSE of 9.4e-2 m. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 6.7e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and read a RMSE of 9.4e-2 m. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 1.2e-2 m, max error 1.7e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 3.5e-3 m, max error 6.0e-3 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 4.9e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The K zones change on column faces. Before 2026-10-09 this strip had one diagonal everywhere: the x conductance came out about 7 % low, which a fixed-head profile hides but a recharge mound shows (5 to 7 cm). The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 4.9e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The K zones change on column faces. Before 2026-10-09 this strip had one diagonal everywhere: the x conductance came out about 7 % low, which a fixed-head profile hides but a recharge mound shows (5 to 7 cm). The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 4.2e-3 m, max error 1.2e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

Steady Boussinesq hillslope-interception benchmark#

pass boussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: the exact steady free-boundary solution under Dupuit. Below the emergence point x_e the head is the land surface and seeps out; above it all the recharge flows through the aquifer and the water table meets the surface tangentially at x_e (322.4 m here).

\[ R\left(x_e-x_{\min}\right)=K\,S\left(z_{\mathrm{top}}(x_e)-z_b\right),\qquad z_{\mathrm{top}}(x)=z_{\mathrm{toe}}+S\left(L-x\right) \]
\[ \left(h-z_b\right)^2=\left(z_{\mathrm{top}}(x_e)-z_b\right)^2+\frac{R}{K}\left[\left(x_e-x_{\min}\right)^2-\left(x-x_{\min}\right)^2\right]\quad (x<x_e),\qquad h=z_{\mathrm{top}}\quad (x\ge x_e) \]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: PETSc VI, the boussinesq variant, against the exact seepage-face solution, started from the outlet head over the whole hillslope. SNESVI converges in 31 iterations (residual 9.8e-11 m3/s). Head profile: RMSE 0.0066 m, max 0.0375 m in the column that holds the tangent point x_e = 322.4 m, the dry zone within 2e-5 m; bounds twice the measurement. The contact point is read on 10 m columns with a 5 cm tolerance, as on the reference (281.6 m): measured 3.4 m off, the bound sits half a column above and fails on the next column. The head may not exceed the land surface by more than the solver closure (1e-6 m). Row spread: 9e-16 m measured, bound 1e-8 m. Until 2026-10-09 the reference ignored the seepage face and the solve started from that reference and stopped at 20 iterations.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The default local engine, regularized partition closure, against the exact seepage-face solution, started from the outlet head over the whole hillslope, with the Newton closure of config_boussinesq_local.toml (1e-8 m3/s): 12 iterations. Head profile: RMSE 0.0071 m, max 0.0375 m in the column that holds the tangent point, as PETSc; the dry heads sit 0.003 m low, the partition releasing a little water where the water table is within a few of its 0.05 m depth scale of the surface. Bounds twice the measurement. The contact point, read on 10 m columns with a 5 cm tolerance as on the reference, is 3.4 m off: the bound sits half a column above. Row spread 1.9e-7 m, bound twice that. The head may not exceed the land surface by more than 1e-6 m. Until 2026-10-10 the release scaled with the saturated share of the cell: RMSE 0.0105 m, dry heads 0.009 m low.

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: exact steady profile H(x) = z_b(x) + b* with b* = 8 m.

\[ H(x)=z_b(x)+b^\ast,\qquad z_b(x)=z_{b,0}+\Delta z_b\left(1-\frac{x-x_{\min}}{L}\right) \]

Steady sloping-substratum fixed-head case#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: steady no-recharge Boussinesq relation on b(x) above a linear substratum, solved through its implicit integral law.

\[ q=K\,b\left(S_0-\frac{\mathrm{d}b}{\mathrm{d}x}\right),\qquad S_0=-\frac{\mathrm{d}z_b}{\mathrm{d}x} \]
\[ x-x_{\min}=\int_{b_w}^{b(x)} \frac{K\,\eta}{K\,\beta\,\eta-q}\,\mathrm{d}\eta,\qquad \beta=S_0,\qquad H(x)=z_b(x)+b(x) \]

Measured on 2026-10-12, commit 427d8bb47 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a4, a local run; 2026-10-13, commit 91d97cabd, version 2.0.0a5, the nightly CI job (job log). The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference, 1.13 to 1.14 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 4.2e-3 m, max error 5.9e-3 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 0.00026 m, max error 0.00049 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and the recharge mound came out 7 cm too high (RMSE 4.5e-2 m): the x conductance was about 7 % low. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 0.00026 m, max error 0.00049 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and the recharge mound came out 7 cm too high (RMSE 4.5e-2 m): the x conductance was about 7 % low. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 7.6e-3 m, max error 1.5e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

Steady circular-island 2D case using the ocean boundary condition#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual sits up to 0.08 m below the reference inside 120 m (radial RMSE 0.067 m), where MODFLOW-NWT on the Cartesian grid sits 0.050 m away. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, so the full-thickness weighting of its Newton conductance is gone. What is left is the saturation of the upstream cell, first order on 625 cells whose node rings are 10 to 30 m apart: without Newton the same input files give 0.003 m, the heads within 4 mm of the reference.

Compared with: steady radial Dupuit-Boussinesq solution with fixed coastal head.

\[ \frac{1}{r}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}r}\left(r\,K\,H\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}r}\right)+R=0 \]
\[ H(r)^2=H(a)^2+\frac{R}{2K}\left(a^2-r^2\right) \]
\[ h(r)=z_b+\sqrt{\left(h_{\mathrm{sea}}-z_b\right)^2+\frac{R}{2K}\left(a^2-r^2\right)} \]

Measured on 2026-10-12, commit 427d8bb47 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a4, a local run; 2026-10-13, commit 91d97cabd, version 2.0.0a5, the nightly CI job (job log). The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference, 2.79 to 3.01 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc (SNESVI obstacle) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.033 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.055 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.90 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m, a node ring on the coast and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. Until 2026-10-09 it was a ring mesh of 18 sectors cut along one diagonal: there the two-point flux sat 0.25 m high with the reference imposed beyond 180 m, and refining that mesh made it worse (+1.1 m at 1476 and 5832 cells), while near-equilateral meshes converge (+0.08, +0.07, +0.02 m at 257, 886, 3147 cells). Half of its ocean triangles were capped at the sea floor (-1 m), a coastal sink that hid most of that bias.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine (scipy_sparse on 3147 cells) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.033 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.055 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.90 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m, a node ring on the coast and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. Until 2026-10-09 it was a ring mesh of 18 sectors cut along one diagonal: there the two-point flux sat 0.25 m high with the reference imposed beyond 180 m, and refining that mesh made it worse (+1.1 m at 1476 and 5832 cells), while near-equilateral meshes converge (+0.08, +0.07, +0.02 m at 257, 886, 3147 cells). Half of its ocean triangles were capped at the sea floor (-1 m), a coastal sink that hid most of that bias.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 10 m grid: radial RMSE 0.0499 m, max error 0.0921 m, spread 0.112 m, and half the measured freeboard of 0.787 m. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell of the layer the same thickness, so its Newton conductance is the one of MODFLOW-NWT, and the two sit at the same distance from the reference (NWT 0.0495 m). What is left is the error of the grid. On a 5 m grid the RMSE falls to 0.0349 m and the max error to 0.0606 m, for MF6 and NWT alike; the spread stays at 0.111 m and the freeboard drops to 0.69 m, the first land ring being closer to the coast. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM, the conductance followed the full thickness of the cells, and the RMSE was 0.221 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: radial RMSE 0.067 m, max error 0.080 m, freeboard 1.90 m. Twice the azimuthal spread of 9.9e-5 m: every cell of the coast ring holds the sea level, so the rings are symmetric. The run reads a 1 m raster whose shoreline lies 1 m inside the coast ring (config_modflow6_voronoi.toml). The profile is read on the node rings (5 m bins). The freeboard is read on the land surface the run was given, at the 196 m ring. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM and the RMSE 0.102 m. Twice the error would let that bias back unnoticed, hence the 10 % margin.
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow_nwt allows 0.25, 5 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.25, 5 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow_nwt allows 0.5, 8 times the 0.066 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.5, 8 times the 0.066 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow_nwt allows 0.25, 1250 times the 0.0002 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.25, 1250 times the 0.0002 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.

What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.

Steady Dupuit seepage limit and its invariance in K/R#

pass end to endmodflow6

Compared with: Dupuit seepage limit x_e = L / (1 + slope**2 K/R) and the free Dupuit water table above it.

\[ x_e=\frac{L}{1+s^2\,K/R} \]
\[ h(x)=s\,x \quad (x<x_e),\qquad h(x)^2=(s\,x_e)^2+\frac{2R}{K}\left(L\,(x-x_e)-\frac{x^2-x_e^2}{2}\right) \quad (x\ge x_e) \]

\(s\) is the slope of the surface, \(L\) the length of the hillslope, \(x\) the distance upslope from the toe, \(K\) the hydraulic conductivity and \(R\) the recharge.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Three claims, in decreasing order of importance:

1. the seepage mask starts where the Dupuit closed form says it does, 2. scaling K and R by the same factor leaves the mask identical cell for cell and the head equal to a tight band - the property the whole calibration method rests on, 3. the same factor on K alone moves the mask, while the total drain discharge does not move at all.

Claim 3 is why claim 2 never looks at the discharge: mass balance pins the total drain outflow at R * area whatever the conductance does, so a discharge-based invariance check passes on a model that ignores K entirely.

Schedule. modflow_nwt, modflow6, modflow6_no_newton: runs in Nightly / validation no PETSc, Weekly / Cross Platform. Jobs.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The case runs through the launcher, the route of test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py, on copies of its configuration refined twice by 2 (cells of 25, 12.5 and 6.25 m). The slope of the head RMSE against the cell size is the observed order of the scheme.

Without Newton, MODFLOW 6 takes the harmonic mean of the two cell transmissivities, a centred scheme of order 2. A head posed half a cell away from where the reference expects it adds an error of order 1 and drops the observed order to 1. This is the check the MMS tests cannot make: they import nothing from hydromodpy.

Under Newton, the HydroModPy default, MODFLOW 6 weights the saturated thickness of the upstream cell, and so does MODFLOW-NWT. That scheme is of order 1 by construction: the RMSE halves when the cells halve (13.3, 6.7 and 3.4 mm here). Both runs are checked against order 1.

Every run closes the head to 1e-9 m, far below the discretization error, so the observed order is the order of the scheme. The bands are those of the MMS orders, |p - 2| < 0.2 and |p - 1| < 0.2 (tests/TOLERANCES.md).

The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

With a head closure of 1e-6 m the RMSE goes from 2.7e-4 m on this strip to 1.2e-4 m on a mesh of 1588 triangles, and the max error from 6.1e-4 m to 5.2e-4 m, then in the first bin, next to the fixed head. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Same closed form as the kernel-level unit test (tests/unit/physics/test_an_impulse_through_the_transit_store_follows_the_exponential_reservoir.py), but reached the way a run reaches it: through compute_soil_forcings, with a single SAFRAN cell's precipitation and ETP passed in as FieldRecord and the recharge read back from the FieldRecord it returns.

spinup = "none" starts the soil full - "the state of a soil in a wet winter", its own description says - which is exactly the soil a year of rain has already filled. Section 7 gives the closed form for a pulse landing on that full soil and then routed through a linear reservoir of time constant k: Q(0) = 50(1 - k a), Q(t>=1) = 50 k a^2 exp(-(t-1)/k) with a = 1 - exp(-1/k). t95, the day the cumulative recharge first reaches 95 % of the 50 mm pulse, follows the continuous crossing -k ln(0.05) within the one day the discretisation can miss it by.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 82: Soil transit store impulse volume, |sum_t Q - 50| over 60 k days, mm: 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. The tail beyond 60 k days holds 50 exp(-60), below 1e-24 mm)
  • Row 86: Routed impulse validation case, t95 against -k ln 0.05, days: 1 (Discretisation. Daily steps: the cumulative recharge crosses 95 % within the day that follows the continuous crossing)

Thin-aquifer Brutsaert recession benchmark#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: nonlinear late recession of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977) for a strip drained on one side, Q(t) = (Q*^(-1/2) + a t / 2)^(-2).

\[ -\frac{dQ}{dt}=a\,Q^{3/2},\qquad Q(t)=\left(Q_*^{-1/2}+\frac{a\,t}{2}\right)^{-2},\qquad a=\frac{C\,\sqrt{K}\,W}{S_y\,(B\,W)^{3/2}} \]

\(K\) is the hydraulic conductivity, \(S_y\) the specific yield, \(B\) the drainage length, \(W\) the outlet width and \(C = 3\,I^{3/2} = 2.4025\) with \(I=\int_0^1 p\,(1-p^3)^{-1/2}\,dp\). Twice \(C\) is the 4.804 of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977), written for a channel drained from both banks (validation_cases/analytical/transient/brutsaert_reference.py).

Deep-aquifer Brutsaert recession benchmark#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: linearized Boussinesq recession of a deep strip after steady recharge, whose tail is the exponential law of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977).

\[ Q(t)=Q_0\,\frac{B}{B-d}\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{8\cos\!\left(\frac{k\pi d}{2B}\right)}{k^2\pi^2}\,e^{-k^2 a t},\qquad k=2n-1,\qquad a=\frac{\pi^2\,K\,D}{4\,S_y\,B^2} \]

\(Q_0\) is the steady discharge at the end of the warm-up, \(K\) the hydraulic conductivity, \(S_y\) the specific yield, \(D\) the saturated thickness at the outlet, \(B\) the drainage length and \(d\) the length near the outlet that the model does not recharge. The first term alone is the late exponential law (validation_cases/analytical/transient/brutsaert_reference.py).

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

With no advection and no dispersion, a uniform initial concentration decays as C(t) = C0 * exp(-k t) under the MF6 MST first-order decay term. The MF6 GWT clock is SECONDS, so the decay rate k is in 1/s. This guards the per-second unit contract for transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.rate_decay: a per-day value would be ~86400x too large and annihilate the solute.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 35: max relative concentration error < 1 % (decay is exact in MST; the allowance covers finite time-stepping).

Growth of a groundwater mound under a rectangle of recharge against Hantush (1967)#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: Hantush (1967) mound under a rectangle of uniform recharge, linearized with the mean saturated thickness b = (hi + hm(t)) / 2 taken at the centre hm, solved at each time; S* integrated with scipy.integrate.quad_vec. Carleton (2010, USGS SIR 2010-5102) gives the same form.

\[ h^2-h_i^2=\frac{w}{2K}\,\nu t\left[S^*\!\left((l+x)n,(a+y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l+x)n,(a-y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l-x)n,(a+y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l-x)n,(a-y)n\right)\right] \]
\[ S^*(\alpha,\beta)=\int_0^1\operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)\operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)d\tau,\qquad \nu=\frac{K\bar b}{S_y},\qquad n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\nu t}},\qquad \bar b=\frac{h_i+h_m(t)}{2} \]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured against the Hantush mound on the 101 x 101 grid of 20 m with steps of 6 h, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: transect space-time RMSE 1.6e-3 m, max error 4.8e-3 m (the centre at day 3), final transect RMSE 1.3e-3 m, final map max 5.4e-3 m, for a mound of 0.75 m. Refined with MODFLOW 6, steps of 3 and 1 h read RMSE 9.5e-4 and 9.1e-4 m on 20 m cells, the floor of the 20 m grid; cells of 6.7 m read 2.0e-3 m with 6 h steps and 4.2e-4 m with 1 h steps (max 1.2e-3 m). That limit is the linearization: a nonlinear finite-difference solution on 6.7 m cells and 45 min steps reads 3.5e-4 m and 1.1e-3 m against the reference.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc TS VI (4 backward-Euler steps a period) on the conforming triangles of the MODFLOW 6 triangle grid: transect space-time RMSE 1.1e-3 m, max error 4.7e-3 m, centre max 2.2e-3 m, final transect RMSE 1.8e-3 m, final map max 9.0e-3 m. The map max sits in the cells where MODFLOW 6 reads its own on these triangles, 20 to 40 m outside the long sides of the rectangle.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on these 6806 conforming triangles with one backward-Euler step a period: transect space-time RMSE 1.37e-3 m, max error 4.6e-3 m, centre max 4.4e-3 m, final transect RMSE 1.2e-3 m, final map max 1.04e-2 m. MODFLOW 6 on the same triangles reads the same within 4 %, and its refinement converges to Hantush: the error is the mesh and the step. The run stores the whole recharge, 0.99999999 of the recharged volume. Until 2026-10-10 the surface closure released 3.6 % of the recharge with the water table 10 m under the top, and the mound ended 1.7 cm low.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the conforming triangles, 6806 cells of 10 m under the rectangle and up to 80 m at the sides, whose edges follow the rectangle so each triangle takes all or none of the recharge: transect space-time RMSE 1.4e-3 m, max error 4.7e-3 m, centre max 4.6e-3 m, final transect RMSE 1.2e-3 m. The final map max, 1.0e-2 m, sits 20 to 40 m outside the long sides, where triangles of 12 m meet the recharge edge: the two-point flux between centroids is not consistent on a general triangle, and the Boussinesq runtime on the same triangles reads the same cells.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual, 3556 cells centred on nodes that face each other across the rectangle edges, so each cell takes all or none of the recharge: transect space-time RMSE 2.0e-3 m, max error 5.3e-3 m (the centre at day 3.75), final transect RMSE 2.0e-3 m, final map max 4.5e-3 m. The dual is K-orthogonal: its map error stays at the level of the structured grid.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured against the Theis drawdown, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 4.4e-3 m, max error 9.8e-3 m, final RMSE 5.3e-3 m. The azimuthal spread bound is ten times the MODFLOW 6 head closure, 1e-6 m: the grid is symmetric about the well. Until 2026-10-09 the reference evaluated E1 by an asymptotic series that is wrong between u = 1 and 8, which doubled the space-time error at the outer monitor points.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: About twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on the 10082 triangles of 71 x 71 squares (397 m2, the cell area of the MODFLOW grid) with one backward-Euler step a period: space-time RMSE 0.0048 m, max error 0.0140 m, final RMSE 0.0035 m, final max error 0.0045 m, azimuthal spread 0.0012 m. MODFLOW on its 101 x 101 grid, with the same single step a period, reads a space-time RMSE of 0.0044 m: the error is the time step and the fixed-transmissivity Theis reference. The reference is read at the centroid of the triangle each monitor point reads, with the well at the centroid of the triangle that holds it, 6.6 m off the well point. Read from the well point, that offset alone gave an azimuthal spread of 0.136 m on the former 31 x 31 mesh. Until 2026-10-10 the surface closure sent up to 3.4 m3/day of the pumping out of the well cell, 10 m under the top: space-time RMSE 0.0043 m, final max error 0.0064 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the refined triangle mesh: space-time RMSE 4.4e-3 m, max error 1.45e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max error 5.0e-3 m, azimuthal spread 0.020 m. The reference is read at the centroid of the triangle each monitor point reads, with the well at the centroid of the triangle that holds it. The well point is a mesh node, and MODFLOW 6 puts the well in the first triangle that holds it, whose centroid lies 15.4 m away: read from the well point, that offset gave an azimuthal spread of 0.087 m. The spread left, 0.020 m at 60 m where the drawdown is 0.85 m, is the asymmetry of the gmsh refinement (165 to 221 triangles per quadrant within 300 m).
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual of the refined mesh, the reference read at the node of the cell each monitor point reads: space-time RMSE 9.4e-3 m, max error 2.3e-2 m, final RMSE 6.3e-3 m, final max error 7.7e-3 m, azimuthal spread of the error 2.2e-3 m. A node sits on the well, so the cell that holds the well is centred on it. Read at the monitor radius instead, 1 to 18 m from that node, the error was twice as large. Until 2026-10-10 the spread was taken on the drawdown, not on the error, and read 0.040 m: the cells read sit at different radii.

Compared with: Ferris (1951) tidal propagation into a semi-infinite linearized unconfined aquifer, T = K b with the saturated thickness b, S = Sy.

\[ S_y\frac{\partial h}{\partial t}=T\frac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x^2},\qquad h(0,t)=h_0+A\cos\left(\frac{2\pi t}{t_0}\right) \]
\[ h(x,t)=h_0+A\,e^{-x/\lambda}\cos\left(\frac{2\pi t}{t_0}-\frac{x}{\lambda}\right),\qquad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{t_0\,T}{\pi\,S_y}} \]

Measured on 2026-10-12, commit 427d8bb47 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a4, a local run; 2026-10-13, commit 91d97cabd, version 2.0.0a5, the nightly CI job (job log). The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference over space and time, 0.46 to 0.5 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid of 2 m over the last four tides, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 5.3e-3 m, max error 3.3e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max 1.0e-2 m; decay length 11.03 m and lag length 12.63 m against 11.73 m, errors of 6.0 % and 7.7 %. The error is backward Euler with one step per hourly period, 24 a tide: theory shortens the decay length and stretches the lag length by about w dt / 4 = 6.5 %. Periods of 4, 2 and 1 h give a space-time RMSE of 2.0e-2, 1.0e-2 and 5.3e-3 m, and lag-length errors of 45, 17 and 7.7 %; 16 sub-steps a period bring the decay and lag errors to 0.9 and 1.7 %, and 100 columns change the RMSE by 5 %. The max error sits in the sea column, which holds the mean tide of each hour while the reference holds the tide at the output time: A w dt / 2 = 3.3e-2 m. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 50 x 5 square cells of 2 m split into triangles: space-time RMSE 3.5e-3 m, max error 2.9e-2 m, final RMSE 1.1e-3 m, final max 2.8e-3 m; decay and lag length errors 1.9 and 2.5 %. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI), and MODFLOW 6 with 4 sub-steps a period reads 2.0 and 2.8 % on the same tide, so the error is first order in time. The max error sits in the sea column, which holds the mean tide of each hour. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads 1e-15 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on these 500 triangles with one backward-Euler step a period: space-time RMSE 5.1e-3 m, max error 3.1e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max 1.0e-2 m; decay and lag length errors 5.9 and 7.5 %, the MODFLOW values of tolerances.toml, where the error is explained. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the sparse engine reads 4e-11 m; the bound is 1e-7 m, as on the sibling strips.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the triangle strip of 1446 cells about 1.5 m across, the sea head posed at the mean centroid of the triangles on the west face: space-time RMSE 4.9e-3 m, max error 2.9e-2 m, final RMSE 3.5e-3 m, final max 1.0e-2 m; decay and lag length errors 6.0 and 7.1 %. As on the structured grid, the error is backward Euler with one step per hourly period (see tolerances.toml). The row spread is zero by construction: the loader collapses the strip to one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual of the triangle strip, 763 cells centred on the nodes, the sea head held on the nodes of the west face and the reference read at the node of each cell: space-time RMSE 6.4e-3 m, max error 3.6e-2 m, final RMSE 5.9e-3 m, final max 1.8e-2 m; decay and lag length errors 5.9 and 7.2 %. The decay and lag match the other grids, so the error is backward Euler with one step per hourly period (see tolerances.toml); the dual cells are twice as large as the triangles, which adds to the RMSE. The row spread is zero by construction: the comparison bins the cells into one profile.

Linearized unconfined transient cases against their analytical references#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_localpetsc_ts_vi_obstaclepetsc_vi_obstacle

Compared with: linearized 1D unconfined response to a piecewise west-boundary series; linearized 1D unconfined response to a step of the west boundary head; linearized 1D unconfined response to a sinusoidal recharge; linearized 1D unconfined response to a recharge step; linearized 1D unconfined response to a recharge step in a deep aquifer, where the linearization error is smaller.

Case lu_boundary_piecewise_1d

\[ S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2},\qquad \eta(L,t)=0 \]
\[ \eta(x,t)=\sum_k \Delta h_k\,\eta_{\mathrm{step}}(x,t-t_k)\,H(t-t_k) \]

Case lu_boundary_step_1d

\[ S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2},\qquad \eta(0,t)=\Delta h\,H(t),\qquad \eta(L,t)=0 \]
\[ \eta(x,t)=\Delta h\left[1-\frac{x}{L}-\frac{2}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin\left(n\pi x/L\right)}{n}\exp\left(-D\left(n\pi/L\right)^2 t\right)\right] \]

Case lu_recharge_periodic_1d

\[ S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2}+R(t),\qquad h=h_0+\eta \]
\[ R(t)=\overline{R}+A\sin\left(2\pi t/P+\phi\right) \]

Case lu_recharge_step_1d

\[ S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2}+R_0\,H(t),\qquad h=h_0+\eta \]
\[ \eta(x,t)=\frac{R_0}{2T_0}x(L-x)-\frac{4R_0L^2}{T_0\pi^3}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\sin\left((2n+1)\pi x/L\right)}{(2n+1)^3}\exp\left(-D\left((2n+1)\pi/L\right)^2 t\right) \]

Case lu_recharge_step_deep_1d

\[ S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2}+R_0\,H(t),\qquad h=h_0+\eta \]
\[ T_0=K\,h_{\mathrm{ref}},\qquad D=\frac{T_0}{S_y} \]

Measured on 2026-10-12, commit 427d8bb47 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a4, a local run; 2026-10-13, commit 91d97cabd, version 2.0.0a5, the nightly CI job (job log). The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference over space and time, 0.0137 to 0.3 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6, petsc_ts_vi_obstacle, petsc_vi_obstacle: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 6.1e-3 m, max error 3.3e-2 m, final RMSE 2.8e-3 m. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 50 x 5 square cells of 2 m: space-time RMSE 0.0016 m, max error 0.0082 m, final RMSE 0.00071 m. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI); the error is first order in time, so it sits below the one-step MODFLOW band of this case. The heads sit dx/3 inside the faces. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The band of tolerances.toml, shared with MODFLOW. On this 500-cell strip the default 'auto' engine runs scipy_sparse, one backward-Euler step a period as MODFLOW does, and on 50 x 5 square cells of 2 m it reads space-time RMSE 0.0061 m, max error 0.033 m, final RMSE 0.0027 m, against 6.1e-3, 3.3e-2 and 2.8e-3 m for MODFLOW. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the sparse engine reads 3e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the triangle strip: space-time RMSE 6.1e-3 m, max error 3.3e-2 m, final RMSE 2.9e-3 m. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader collapses the strip to one profile. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centres of the boundary cells.
  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 1.4e-3 m, max error 1.2e-2 m, final RMSE 9.0e-5 m. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 40 x 4 square cells of 2.5 m: space-time RMSE 0.00034 m, max error 0.0032 m, final RMSE 7.3e-05 m. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI); the error is first order in time, so it sits below the one-step MODFLOW band of this case. The heads sit dx/3 inside the faces. Before 2026-10-09 the 40-column strips had 3 rows, cells of 2.5 x 3.3 m: on right triangles of unequal sides the two-point flux of the solver is not consistent, and the recharge step ended 1.1e-2 m off. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The band of tolerances.toml, shared with MODFLOW. The default local engine takes one backward-Euler step a period, as MODFLOW does, and on 40 x 4 square cells of 2.5 m it reads space-time RMSE 0.0014 m, max error 0.012 m, final RMSE 9.9e-05 m, against 1.4e-3, 1.2e-2 and 9.0e-5 m for MODFLOW. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the triangle strip: space-time RMSE 1.4e-3 m, max error 1.2e-2 m, final RMSE 1.5e-4 m. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader collapses the strip to one profile. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centres of the boundary cells.
  • Thresholds of petsc_ts_vi_obstacle: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 40 x 4 square cells of 2.5 m: space-time RMSE 0.00034 m, max error 0.0032 m, final RMSE 7.3e-05 m. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI); the error is first order in time, so it sits below the one-step MODFLOW band of this case. The heads sit dx/3 inside the faces. What the test does, all thresholds, the file

This driver folds five sibling 1D linearized-unconfined transient benchmarks into one parametrized suite. Each scenario keeps its own forcing (via its own launcher comparison function) and its own tolerances (read from the per-case tolerance TOML through the comparison payload). The references pose the side heads where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

For a constant-gradient (uniform) flow field, Pollock's method is exact, so a particle moves as x(t) = x0 + v*t with v = q / porosity (q is the specific discharge). The pore velocity v is read back from the model's DATA-SPDIS instead of being hard-coded, then the track positions are checked against the analytical streamline.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 34: max relative position error < 1 % (Pollock is exact for uniform velocity; the allowance covers cell-crossing arithmetic).

Compared with: Glover and Balmer (1954) stream depletion and the image-well Theis drawdown (Theis 1941), with T = K b and S = Sy, read at the stream, well and monitor cell centres.

\[ \frac{Q_s}{Q}=\operatorname{erfc}\left(\sqrt{\frac{S a^2}{4 T t}}\right) \]
\[ s(x,y,t)=\frac{Q}{4\pi T}\left[E_1\left(\frac{r_1^2 S}{4 T t}\right)-E_1\left(\frac{r_2^2 S}{4 T t}\right)\right] \]
\[ T=K\,b,\qquad S=S_y \]

a is the distance from the well to the stream, r1 the distance to the well and r2 the distance to its image across the stream.

Until 2026-10-10 the run stored the depletion of the last step and the reference was read at the period end: 0.0083 at most. The drawdown error is the grid and the unconfined flow: on a 5 m grid the RMSE halves, and at a tenth of the pumping rate the final error near the well falls from 3.6e-3 to 2.2e-4 m, the s^2 / (2 b) of the water table. The closed sides do not count: on a domain 1.5 times wider and longer the results move by 6e-6. What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A stress period holds a constant forcing, and HydroModPy stores only its end state. Against the closed form of a step at a Dirichlet boundary, h(x, t) = dh * erfc(x / (2 sqrt(D t))) with D = K b / S, this case pins three statements that are easy to get backwards:

1. simulation.time.substeps_per_period is the knob. The default of one backward-Euler step over the whole period carries an order of magnitude more error than ten. 2. A geometric partition (MODFLOW TSMULT) cannot help. Within a period the forcing is constant, so the backward-Euler end state is a commuting product over the steps: it depends on the multiset of step sizes and not on their order, and equal steps minimise its error. A growth ratio and its reciprocal give the same error, both worse than equal steps. This is why HydroModPy declares TSMULT = 1 and exposes no growth field. 3. Adaptive time stepping must not undo the request. MF6 ignores the TDIS NSTP of a period ATS covers, so the ATS record has to carry the declared step as both its starting and its maximum value.

A fourth test leaves the closed form for HydroModPy's own configuration, a seasonal recharge on a hillslope drained by surface DRN cells and a river. There the default of one step per period is not a small bias: it moves the monthly discharge, the quantity a calibration scores against, by tens of percent. The default is left at 1 because the right count is a property of the model (tau = L**2 S / (K b) against the period length) and the cost is linear in it, but a run that leaves it there is making a choice, not accepting a neutral value.

Tolerances: tests/TOLERANCES.md rows 65-68.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 65: Stress-period sub-stepping (MF6), RMSE ratio between nstp=1 and nstp=10: > 10x (Derived. Backward Euler is first order in time, so halving the step halves the error; ten steps should gain about an order of magnitude on a smooth relaxation, and the assertion is the weakest form of that (a strict factor 10) rather than a fitted ratio)
  • Row 66: Stress-period sub-stepping (MF6), RMSE difference between TSMULT r and 1/r: 1e-6 m (Derived. Within a stress period the forcing is constant, so the backward-Euler end state is a product of commuting operators over the steps: it depends on the multiset of step sizes and not on their order, and a ratio and its reciprocal only reverse that order. The identity is exact in exact arithmetic, so the band is the iterative closure, declared at DVCLOSE = 1e-3 m by COMPLEXITY SIMPLE)
  • Row 67: Adaptive time stepping (MF6), RMSE relative difference, ATS on against ATS off: 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. Nothing fails on this column, so ATS never cuts, and with dt0 = dtmax = perlen / nstp it replays the declared partition step for step. The two runs are the same arithmetic in the same order)
  • Row 68: One step per stress period (MF6), monthly discharge drift against a refined run: 0.10 (Derived. Backward Euler is first order, so the drift scales with the step; on the hillslope this case builds it is measured at 28 % with one step per month against thirty, and it stays above 10 % across the whole plausible bedrock range (K from 1e-7 to 1e-4 m/s gave 4 % to 28 %). The floor is set at 10 %, well inside the measured band, because the row exists to state that the drift is large and not to pin its exact value)

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A fully penetrating well pumps at constant rate Q in a confined aquifer overlain by a leaky aquitard of thickness b' and vertical conductivity K'. A source bed of constant head sits above the aquitard. Under these assumptions the analytical drawdown is the Hantush solution:

s(r, t) = Q / (4 pi T) * W(u, r / B)

with u = r^2 S / (4 T t), B = sqrt(T b' / K') the leakage factor and the Hantush well function

W(u, beta) = int_u^inf (1/y) exp(-y - beta^2 / (4 y)) dy.

The numerical reference is a three-layer MF6 IMS model:

* layer 0: source bed - all cells are CHD at the initial head,
* layer 1: aquitard - thickness ``b'`` and K = ``K'``, no storage,
* layer 2: main pumped aquifer - thickness ``b``, K such that
``T = K b``, specific storage such that ``S = S_s b``.

A telescoping grid concentrates resolution near the well; the outer Dirichlet ring sits well beyond the radius of influence ~sqrt(4 T t / S). Drawdown is compared at radii 10/50/100 m and times 1/3/10 d.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 6: NSE > 0.99 and maximum pointwise relative error below 2 %.

Scope - solver_sanity: The three-layer sandwich (source / aquitard / pumped aquifer) and the telescoping grid are built directly on the flopy SDK because the hydromodpy launcher TOML does not expose this geometry. The test therefore validates MODFLOW 6 against the Hantush analytical solution, not the hydromodpy pipeline.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A semi-infinite column is initially solute-free and subjected to a constant-concentration injection c0 at x = 0 under steady uniform flow of pore velocity v with longitudinal dispersion coefficient D. The analytical solution is the Ogata-Banks profile:

c(x, t) = c0 / 2 * [ erfc((x - v t) / (2 sqrt(D t)))
                    + exp(v x / D) * erfc((x + v t) / (2 sqrt(D t))) ]

The reference is a 1D MF6 GWF + GWT model: flow is driven by a constant injection flux on the left and a CHD sink on the right producing a uniform pore velocity v; transport is solved with a constant concentration c0 at the inlet and an open boundary at the outlet. Numerical and analytical concentrations are compared at probe points along the column at three times.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 7: NSE > 0.95 across all (x, t) probes with a maximum pointwise relative error below 2.5 % (measured 2.2 % at the production grid). A second test refines dt by 4 and dx by 2 and requires the error to fall below that of the production run.

Scope - solver_sanity: The coupled GWF + GWT column with inlet auxiliary concentration is built directly on the flopy SDK because hydromodpy's transport plumbing does not yet expose MF6 GWT through the launcher TOML. The test therefore validates MODFLOW 6 GWT against the Ogata-Banks analytical solution, not the hydromodpy pipeline.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A fully penetrating well pumps at a constant rate Q in a homogeneous isotropic confined aquifer of transmissivity T and storativity S. The drawdown field is radial:

s(r, t) = Q / (4 pi T) * W(u),  u = r^2 S / (4 T t)

with well function W(u) = E_1(u) (exponential integral). The numerical reference is an MF6 IMS-backed confined GWF model. The grid is telescoping - a fine inner patch resolves the near-well drawdown and coarse outer cells push the Dirichlet boundary far enough that its influence on the observation window stays well below the test tolerance. Drawdown is evaluated at three radial distances (10 m, 50 m, 100 m) and three times (1 d, 3 d, 10 d) and compared pointwise against s(r, t).

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md rows 4/5: * NSE against analytical drawdown must exceed 0.999. * Maximum absolute error across all (r, t) pairs: 1% relative.

Scope - solver_sanity: The model is built directly on the flopy SDK (telescoping grid, central well, outer CHD ring) because the geometry sits outside what the hydromodpy launcher TOML exposes. This test therefore validates MODFLOW 6 against the Theis analytical solution, not the hydromodpy pipeline. It protects against solver-level regressions and bundled-binary drift, not against hydromodpy refactors.

Patch test: a uniform flow on skewed triangles#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow6_irregular_triboussinesq_localmodflow6_irregular_tri_xt3d_off

Known gap: modflow6_irregular_tri_xt3d_off

The two-point flux is not consistent on these triangles. It takes the flux across an edge as T L (h_b - h_a) / d, d the distance between the two cell centres: that is the flux of a uniform gradient only where the centre line is normal to the edge. On this strip the angle between them has a median of 23 deg and a 95th percentile of 42 deg, so a linear head does not balance and the solution bends: 3 to 6 % of the head drop. Control run, the same files with XT3D: 6e-8 m. The error does not fall with the cell size: the Boussinesq solver, which has the same flux, reads 5.8e-3, 5.6e-3 and 5.5e-3 m RMSE on 80, 320 and 1280 triangles of the same shapes. Gmsh catchment meshes have such angles; HydroModPy switches XT3D on by itself when their 95th percentile passes 30 deg.

Known gap: boussinesq_local

The Boussinesq solver has a two-point flux between triangle centroids, T L (h_b - h_a) / d, d the distance between the centroids, with no correction for skewed cells. It is the flux of a uniform gradient only where the centroid line is normal to the edge. On this strip the angle between them has a median of 23 deg and a 95th percentile of 42 deg, so a linear head does not balance and the solution bends: 3 to 6 % of the head drop, as for MODFLOW 6 with XT3D off (5.7e-3 m). The error does not fall with the cell size: 5.8e-3, 5.6e-3 and 5.5e-3 m RMSE on 80, 320 and 1280 triangles of the same shapes, the mark of an inconsistent scheme. MODFLOW 6 with XT3D reproduces the head to 6e-8 m. A Gmsh catchment mesh has such angles; the island cases mesh near-equilateral triangles for this reason.

Compared with: the steady head of a uniform flow at every triangle centroid.

\[ \left(h(x)-z_b\right)^2=\left(h_W-z_b\right)^2+\left[\left(h_E-z_b\right)^2-\left(h_W-z_b\right)^2\right]\frac{x-x_W}{x_E-x_W} \]

  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Derived. XT3D reconstructs the gradient from the neighbours and is exact for a uniform flow on any cell shape: what is left is the solver closure (outer dvclose 1e-9 m) and the spread of the transmissivity, 2e-4 across the strip, which moves the exact head off a straight line by 5e-6 m. The bound is twice that. Measured: RMSE 2.3e-8 m, max 5.8e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri_xt3d_off: 1.1 times the measurement, a documented gap (below): RMSE 0.0057 m, max error 0.0120 m, for a head drop of 0.2 m across the strip.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The SAME transient multi-layer lake-aquifer problem (Plainfield Lakes abacus, one reservoir incised across the top two layers of a 4-layer aquifer) is solved twice through the production HMP LAK builders and MF6:

  • REGULAR: the 15x15 quad DISV (225 cells, 40 m).
  • IRREGULAR: a refined Delaunay TRIANGLE DISV (~772 cells, ~20 m near the lake) over the same domain, layers, lake footprint, abacus, bedleak, aquifer K / recharge, TDIS and per-period rainfall / evaporation / runoff.

Only the mesh changes, so the lake stage and the lake-aquifer exchange flux must agree across grids (grid independence). The test asserts:

  • the irregular grid is a genuine non-rectangular triangulation that resolves the lake at least as finely as the quad grid;
  • the per-period lake stages agree within the documented stage envelope;
  • the steady lake-aquifer exchange flux agrees within the documented envelope;
  • both grids close their LAK water balance.

A materially diverging grid (wrong CONNECTIONDATA geometry, lost bank seepage) would break the stage or exchange envelope by an order of magnitude.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Governing PDE on [0, 1] with Dirichlet 0/0 and initial condition h(x, 0) = sin(pi x):

h_t - D h_xx = 0

The manufactured solution h(x, t) = exp(-pi^2 D t) sin(pi x) is an exact eigenfunction of the Laplacian with no forcing. The discretisation combines the standard second-order centred-space stencil with either backward Euler (first-order in time) or Crank-Nicolson (second-order in time) for the temporal update. Two refinement studies are run:

  • space - dx refined with Crank-Nicolson in time so the temporal error stays small enough for the spatial slope to emerge. Expected slope ~2.
  • time - dx held fine, dt refined under backward Euler. Expected slope ~1 (see tests/TOLERANCES.md row 10).

Scope, read this before citing the result ----------------------------------------- This file imports nothing from hydromodpy. It verifies the *scheme* on a stencil assembled inside the test, which is what MMS is for: it establishes that the discretisation written here converges at its theoretical order. It does not exercise HydroModPy's own assembly, so a passing run here is not evidence that the production discretisation is second-order.

What does cover the production path is the analytical tier (tests/validation/analytical/): Theis, Hantush and Ogata-Banks run a real solve through HydroModPy and compare against a closed form. Those would catch a gross regression, but a silent drop from order 2 to order 1 that stays inside the RMSE band would pass them. Closing that gap means running this convergence study on the production assembly, not extending this file.

  • Mms diffusion transient space converges at order two.
  • Mms diffusion transient time converges at order one.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Manufactured solution on [0, 1] with Dirichlet 0/0 boundaries:

u_exact(x) = sin(pi x)
-u''(x)    = pi^2 sin(pi x) = f(x)

The vertex-centred finite-volume (equivalent to the standard second-order centred finite-difference) stencil is:

(u[i-1] - 2 u[i] + u[i+1]) / h^2 = -f[i]

which is second-order consistent. Running on a sequence of refinements and regressing log ||e||_2 against log h gives an empirical order expected to sit inside [1.8, 2.2] (see tests/TOLERANCES.md row 8).

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A MODFLOW 6 run with K = 1e-4 m/s and Sy = 0.10 under a recharge step gives the head at mid-aquifer and the outlet discharge. Each method then searches K in [5e-5, 3e-4] and Sy in [0.04, 0.18] from those two series alone. This is the one well-posed two-parameter transient calibration of the suite: the head series constrains Sy and the discharge series constrains K. CMA-ES, Nelder-Mead and Optuna are asserted to land within the case tolerance of the truth (1.5e-5 on K, 0.04 on Sy). Random search, GP mapping and DA-MH-GP also run; their distances to the truth are recorded for information and not asserted, because their budget does not guarantee a hit on a smooth two-parameter surface.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A model run with a known conductivity produces a seepage network. That network, written as the mapped one, must bring a network-only bisection back to the conductivity that produced it. Nothing else in the suite runs the criterion end to end on a real solve: the unit tests fake the trial context, and a real catchment has no known answer.

The catchment is a planar hillslope, one row of 400 square cells of 2 m, over a 30 m aquifer parallel to the surface. Under uniform recharge R the water table reaches the surface where the recharge collected upslope exceeds what the full aquifer can carry, K * d * slope: the seepage face starts at about K d s / R from the divide, so the network retracts by one cell per cell / (K d s / R) of relative K, about 0.56 per cent here. That step is the resolution of the criterion. It is kept below the one per cent the bisection stops on, so the recovered value can be held to that one per cent whether the search lands on the zero plateau or closes its bracket around it.

The drains sit on the surface with the fallback conductance, proportional to K, which is what makes the network a function of K/R alone. The mapped network is the downstream closure of the seepage cells, built by the same functions the criterion calls, and its round trip through the GPKG back onto the mesh is checked cell for cell before any calibration runs. The round trip goes through the resolver and observed_network_mask under the crossing rule, the route a stream_geometry_path takes in a calibration trial. The calibration sets that rule: the default, heads, needs a drained area this hillslope never reaches.

What this twin cannot see: on a single row no two network cells meet only at a corner, so the crossing and the touch rules give the same mask here. The diagonal-step bias the crossing rule exists to remove is covered by the unit tests of line_crossing_cell_mask, not by this experiment.

Tolerances: tests/TOLERANCES.md, rows 76 to 79.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 76: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6, planar hillslope, 400 cells of 2 m), |K - K_true| / K_true at the returned trial, and the same on k_over_r against K_true / R: <= 1 % (Derived. The bisection stops on a bracket no wider than log10(1.01). The zero plateau of J, the K range that reproduces the mapped network cell for cell, is one cell over the length of the unsaturated slope, cell / (K d s / R) = 2 m / 357 m = 0.56 %, measured between 5.99e-6 and 6.03e-6 m/s. A returned trial on the plateau is within 0.56 % of K_true; one off it is an end of a closed bracket that holds the plateau, so within 1 %)
  • Row 78: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6), d_sat_m at the returned trial against the truth run: rel <= 1e-3 (Derived. The sweep gives d dsat / d ln K of about 1.06 m around the truth, so 1 % on K moves dsat by 0.011 m, 3.6e-4 of 29.47 m; the band is 2.8 times that)
  • Row 79: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6), k_optim_m_s, k_over_r, t_over_r_m, t_optim_m2_s against K, R_mean_m_s and d_sat_m of the returned trial: rel 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. Each is one product or quotient of values the report read off that trial)

Two solvers on one catchment#

The cases above compare each solver with an exact solution. A catchment has none, so the reference model of example 04 is run twice from the same file: once with MODFLOW 6, once with MODFLOW-NWT. Only the solver of the flow process changes. Both runs store their fields at full precision: the default compact storage rounds these heads to steps of 1 to 2 mm, more than the gap between the two solvers. tools/docs/figures/render_ex04_figures.py (group solvers) makes both runs and draws the figures below; tools/docs/figures/figures.toml keeps the command behind each one.

The aquifer of example 04 has the same thickness in every cell. Where the thickness changes from one cell to the next, MODFLOW 6 under Newton computes another horizontal conductance than MODFLOW-NWT, smaller where water flows from a thicker cell to a thinner one. MODFLOW 6 then reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, and the two solvers agree again: the circular-island cases above show it on the Cartesian grid.
